import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()

    # Extract watermark high_ts (single row)
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]

    # 1. Keep only events with event_ts > watermark.high_ts
    filtered = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()

    # 2. Per product_id, apply the LATEST event by (event_ts, event_seq)
    if not filtered.empty:
        filtered = filtered.sort_values(
            by=["event_ts", "event_seq"], ascending=[True, True]
        )
        latest_idx = filtered.groupby("product_id").tail(1).index
        latest_events = filtered.loc[latest_idx].copy()
    else:
        latest_events = filtered.copy()

    # Build dict of product_id -> event row for quick lookup
    latest_events = latest_events.set_index("product_id", drop=False)

    # Start from target_snapshot indexed by product_id for easy update/delete
    snapshot = target_snapshot.set_index("product_id", drop=False)

    # Determine deletes and upserts
    delete_ids = latest_events.loc[latest_events["op"] == "D", "product_id"].tolist()
    upsert_ids = latest_events.loc[latest_events["op"].isin(["I", "U"]), "product_id"].tolist()

    # Apply deletes: remove products that exist in snapshot and are deleted
    snapshot = snapshot.drop(index=[pid for pid in delete_ids if pid in snapshot.index], errors="ignore")

    # Apply upserts: update existing or insert new rows
    for pid in upsert_ids:
        ev = latest_events.loc[pid]
        name = ev["name"]
        price = ev["price"]
        event_ts = ev["event_ts"]

        if pid in snapshot.index:
            snapshot.at[pid, "name"] = name
            snapshot.at[pid, "price"] = price
            snapshot.at[pid, "last_event_ts"] = event_ts
        else:
            new_row = pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "product_id": [pid],
                    "name": [name],
                    "price": [price],
                    "last_event_ts": [event_ts],
                }
            )
            new_row = new_row.set_index("product_id", drop=False)
            snapshot = pd.concat([snapshot, new_row], axis=0)

    # Reset index and ensure column order matches target_snapshot schema
    snapshot = snapshot.reset_index(drop=True)
    snapshot = snapshot[target_snapshot.columns]

    return {"new_snapshot": snapshot}
